name: Bungalow's Dynamic Campaign Pacific 1985
description:
June 1985. There was no ultimatum. In the small hours of a spring night, Soviet bombers came in low over Okinawa while Chinese assault boats ran for the beaches of Taiwan, and by dawn the war had already been lost in a dozen places at once.

The weeks since have been a long retreat. Seoul, Manila and Singapore have fallen; Kadena and Clark fly the enemy's colours, and the Indonesian islands went without a fight. The Seventh Fleet has pulled back to lick its wounds: Constellation lies at Darwin, the Marines are regrouping on Guam, and only the destroyers of the Japanese Self-Defense Force still hold the home ports; the carrier Midway has put to sea and is racing round Kyushu to meet the enemy.

Now the enemy is coming for Japan itself. In the Korea Strait and the East China Sea a Soviet landing force under Minsk's guns and a Chinese one are closing on Sasebo, and the patrol planes say they will be off the harbour by nightfall. Out in the central Pacific their submarines wait across the lanes every convoy from Pearl Harbor must cross.

You command what is left in the Pacific. Hold Kyushu. Keep the tankers and the ammunition ships coming. Rebuild the fleet, and then take back, island by island, everything they took. The war ends when every base beyond the Russian and Chinese mainland is ours again, or when theirs is the flag over everything we hold outside Australia and Hawaii.

situation: The Soviet Union and the People's Republic of China opened hostilities without warning some weeks ago. In a short campaign they have overrun Taiwan, South Korea, the Ryukyu Islands, the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia and the Indonesian islands.

The north is China's: Chinese forces hold Taiwan, the Ryukyus and Korea, and Chinese fighters fly from Ching Chuan Kang. The south is the Soviets': staging through Cam Ranh Bay, they hold the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia, their fighters fly from Clark and their naval bombers from Tengah.

Seventh Fleet has fallen back to Darwin and east into the Pacific. Midway's group is at sea off southern Kyushu, half a day's steaming from Sasebo; the Japanese flotillas lie at Yokosuka, Sasebo, Maizuru and Kure.
Supply now comes the long way: across the central Pacific from Pearl Harbor, and up from Sydney.
enemy: The enemy is on a war footing. About two thirds of the enemy fleets are believed at sea; the rest lie in Vladivostok, Petropavlovsk and the Chinese ports.
Enemy submarines are believed across our supply lanes in the central Pacific, between Hawaii, Guam and Japan. Treat every convoy route as threatened.
Soviet and Chinese landing forces are at sea. An assault on Kyushu is feared within hours: with a foothold there the enemy would command the Tsushima Strait.
intent: Hold Kyushu. Sasebo is not to be given up while there is a ship to fight for it.
Keep the convoys moving. Without the fuel and weapons from Pearl Harbor and Sydney the fleet cannot fight.
Our submarines behind the enemy's lines are to attack enemy shipping and report enemy movements.
Preserve the carriers, rebuild the fleet, then take back what was lost.
